item.title: Measures of maximal entropy for monotone factors of smooth surface diffeomorphisms
item.description: arXiv:2611.07236v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that a transitive monotone factor of a smooth surface diffeomorphism has a unique measure of maximal entropy whenever its topological entropy is positive. Its entropy is the entropy of a single homoclinic class of the diffeomorphism, and the factor map is a measure-theoretic isomorphism on every ergodic measure with positive entropy of that class. The other homoclinic classes are mapped to periodic orbits. We give an application to the essential factor of a diffeomorphism isotopic to a pseudo-Anosov map ---possibly relative to a finite invariant set--- constructed by Garc\'ia-Sassi \& Tal: the essential factor has a unique measure of maximal entropy, which is Bernoulli and has full support.
item.dc:creator: Sylvain Crovisier, Alejo Garc\'ia-Sassi, Yuri Lima, F\'abio Tal

item.title: Discrete history operators: Exact state-space realization for sequence memory
item.description: arXiv:2611.07396v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A prescribed finite-dimensional analysis of an evolving discrete history need not admit an exact recurrence driven only by its current state and the entering input. We study exact realizations of causal linear discrete history operators (DHOs). Operator factorization and kernel inclusion characterize exact closure, while the cross-projection defect characterizes closure failure for orthonormal analyses. For finite-dimensional history spaces over fixed finite horizons, we distinguish two minimality problems. Reachable task quotients determine the minimum state dimension for preserving prescribed future tasks on reachable histories. Backward invariant envelopes characterize the minimum dimension of exact linear realizations recovering prescribed analyses on full history spaces within the admissible class. The minimum number of additional independent state directions is given by the rank of the propagated closure defect operator restricted to the kernel of the current analysis. For geometrically weighted countable histories, matrix mode transport yields structured exact recurrences and a uniform exponential decay estimate for state transitions. Additional conditions provide uniform Gram bounds and refined decay estimates. A stationary Meixner specialization yields explicit recurrence matrices, an O(N) arithmetic state update, and minimum augmentation dimensions over finite horizons for selected coefficients. Numerical experiments examine recurrence accuracy, state transition bounds, Gram conditions, and minimum realization dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Bin Zhou, Rong Gao, Zhao-Yan Li

item.title: The fixed-point proportion of Latt\`es maps
item.description: arXiv:2611.07816v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: How often does an element of the geometric iterated Galois group of a Latt\`es map fix a vertex of the tree? Let A/K be an abelian variety over a separably closed field of characteristic 0, G <= Aut(A,0) finite, and alpha an isogeny of degree at least 2 normalising G. The Latt\`es map on X=A/G has a preimage tree governed by alpha-power torsion; we determine the fixed-point proportion in every dimension. For zeta in G the weight is the reciprocal of the number of fixed points of zeta in alpha-power torsion (zero if infinite); equivalently, it is a product of p-adic absolute values of determinants on the alpha-active subspaces; for scalar alpha=m the proportion is (1/|G|) times the sum over 1 != zeta in G of the product over p dividing m of the p-adic absolute value of det(1 - zeta | H_1(A,Z)). We deduce positivity and vanishing criteria, prove the groups G_infinity are martingale groups, determine the limit law, and reduce groups with translations to the fixed-origin case. In dimension one we determine ten values for scalar multipliers and nontrivial G <= Aut(E,0), and for the eight quadratic Latt\`es classes the proportions are 1/8, 1/4 and 5/16. Bridy-Jones-Kelsey-Lodge exclude the Latt\`es case from their main theorem; their Theorem 2.5 periodic-point bound is attained, via reductions modulo split primes p = 1 (mod 4), for the map (x^2+a)/(x^2-a), a^2 = -1, and we settle the exceptional case of the Fari\~na-Asategui-Radi conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Xin Li

item.title: Thurston algorithm for real entire maps: existence and uniqueness
item.description: arXiv:2611.07818v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper deals with the real Thurston pullback algorithm for entire maps with finitely many finite singular values, all real. Given a finite forward-invariant marking containing the singular values and satisfying an interval no-Levy-cycle condition, the pullback is shown to have a unique fixed point and it is shown that every orbit converges to it. The resulting entire map uniquely realises the marked dynamics up to positive affine conjugacy. Thus this paper established Thurston realisation and uniqueness in the setting of real entire maps with a finite postsingular set. As usual, the realisation problem reduces to the existence of a fixed point of the Thurston map $T$ which in the real setting acts on a simplex $W$ of dimension $s-2$ if the required postsingular set consists of $s$ points. The key estimate concerns a finite real preimage interval: when its critical multiplicity is bounded and its endpoint values stay separated from the singular values unless they equal to one, its hyperbolic diameter grows at most double-logarithmically as the separation tends to zero. An expansive marking (absence of Levy cycles) then rules out configurations near the boundary of the simplex whose displacement under the Thurston map is at most a fixed multiple of their distance to the boundary. Using a version of the Brouwer fixed point theorem, this immediately implies that the Thurston map $T$ has a fixed point. The argument permits infinitely many real and non-real critical points and different behaviours as the real variable tends to $+\infty$ and $-\infty$. Additional estimates for fixed labelled inverse branches, which are not strictly necessary for the proof of the Main Theorem, are given in the appendices.
item.dc:creator: Sebastian van Strien

item.title: Hausdorff dimension of nonergodic directions in higher genus via effective equidistribution
item.description: arXiv:2611.07833v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For each fixed $g\ge3$, we prove that non-uniquely ergodic directions have Hausdorff dimension $1/2$ on almost every area-one surface in $\mathcal H^{\mathrm{odd}}(g-1,g-1)$ when $g$ is odd, and in $\mathcal H^{\mathrm{nonhyp}}(g-1,g-1)$ when $g$ is even. We construct these directions through cyclic splittings into $g$ slit tori. Effective equidistribution of Lindenstrauss--Mohammadi--Yang supplies sufficiently many children at each normal input. We estimate cusp and periodic-orbit failures with the original branching weights and prove that their total mass loss is summable. The surviving path measure yields the dimension lower bound, also for directions nonergodic for flat area.
item.dc:creator: Yuming Wei

item.title: Generalized Hopf bifurcations: a homological analysis and obstructions to their existence
item.description: arXiv:2611.08002v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A generalized Hopf bifurcation takes place when varying a parameter of a (semi)dynamical system causes an attractor $K$ to become a repeller. In doing so, it expels a (parameter-dependent) family of attractors. In this paper we concentrate on two questions: (1) what do the expelled attractors look like?, and (2) can any attractor $K$ undergo a generalized Hopf bifurcation? Regarding (1), we compute the cohomology of the expelled attractors in terms of the cohomology of $K$; in the case of continuous-time dynamics this can be improved to a computation of their Borsuk shape. As for (2), we show that certain compacta cannot undergo generalized Hopf bifurcations and, when the ambient space has dimension $ \leq 3$, give a complete topological characterization of which can.
item.dc:creator: H\'ector Barge, J. J. S\'anchez-Gabites

item.title: Hypercyclic and topologically transitive semigroups of composition operators (revised and extended version)
item.description: arXiv:2611.08320v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $X$ be a separable locally compact metric space, let $E\neq\{0\}$ be a normed space, and let $G$ be a semigroup of continuous self-maps of $X$. Every $\varphi\in G$ induces the composition operator $C_\varphi f=f\circ\varphi$ on the space $C(X,E)$ of continuous functions endowed with the compact-open topology. We characterize the topological transitivity of the semigroup $\widehat{G}=\{C_\varphi:\varphi\in G\}$ by a condition that combines the run-away property of $G$ with an approximate form of injectivity, and we show that, when $E$ is separable, $\widehat{G}$ is topologically transitive if and only if it is hypercyclic. In particular, if every element of $G$ is one-to-one and $G$ is run-away, then $\widehat{G}$ is topologically transitive, and hypercyclic when $E$ is separable. For a single map $\varphi$ we obtain: $C_\varphi$ is hypercyclic $\iff$ $C_\varphi$ is topologically transitive $\iff$ $\varphi$ is one-to-one and run-away, and $C_\varphi$ is mixing $\iff$ $\varphi$ is one-to-one and strongly run-away. If, moreover, $\varphi$ is an open map (which is automatic on manifolds by invariance of domain), then $C_\varphi$ is Devaney chaotic. On an open interval all of these properties are equivalent to $\varphi$ being one-to-one without fixed points.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: M. Javaheri, Hypercyclic and topologically transitive semigroups of composition operators, Topology Appl. 164 (2014), 105--112
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Javaheri

item.title: From elementary processes to chaos: a discrete-time two-stage contagion model and its continuous limit
item.description: arXiv:2611.08353v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Two-stage contagion, in which adoption requires two successive contacts with adopters, combined with population turnover produces bistability and relaxation oscillations in Katriel's differential-equation model, but no chaos. We derive from the elementary reactions of the process, without reference to the differential equations, a discrete-time model in which the population is updated in rounds of length $\tau$, as in elections, meetings or turns of a game: each individual makes at most one transition per round, events compete as exponential risks, and adoptions take effect from the next round. The model is a Markov chain whose large-population limit is a map $F_\tau$; Katriel's equations are recovered as $\tau\to0$. Taking the probability $p$ of adoption after a single contact as bifurcation parameter, with rates and round length fixed, $F_\tau$ goes from extinction through a window of chaos to a stable equilibrium; for $\beta/\gamma=46$, $\mu/\gamma=0.002$, $\gamma\tau=5.5$ the window is $0.023\le p\le0.056$, bounded by the invasion threshold and by a boundary crisis beyond a subcritical Neimark--Sacker point. One-stage contagion ($p=1$), $p=0$ and permanent adoption showed no chaos. The chaotic attractor is essentially unique, with one positive Lyapunov exponent and an outbreak--recharge geometry. In the same window Katriel's equations have a periodic relaxation cycle with troughs of $10^{-44}$--$10^{-164}$: the round structure does not create the oscillation but turns it into chaos and shrinks the oscillatory range in $p$ from $(0.022,0.41)$ to $(0.022,0.056)$. The chaos is therefore not an artefact of discretising a stable state, but a property of two-stage contagion with synchronous updating.
item.dc:creator: Francisco J. Mu\~noz, Juan Carlos Nu\~no, Luca Meacci

item.title: Modelling and analysis of a cocktail phage therapy with coinfection
item.description: arXiv:2611.08370v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We analyze a delay differential model for phage therapy in which a cocktail of $n$ different types of bacteriophages, each with its own latency period, is administered and coinfection is allowed. We prove the global existence, uniqueness and nonnegativity of solutions, and the existence of an invariant region, under suitable conditions, in which the bacteria are eradicated exponentially fast. We determine the stability of the bacteria-free equilibrium in terms of the administered doses and give sufficient conditions for the nonexistence of coexistence equilibria, showing that coinfection may allow bacteria and phages to coexist even when the doses are large. For a cocktail of two phage types with the same latency period, we obtain a complete description of the biologically feasible coexistence equilibria, which may be zero, one or two. Numerical simulations illustrate the theoretical results.
item.dc:creator: Xavier Bardina, Marc Cano, Silvia Cuadrado

item.title: Space of Geometric Gibbs Measures: Uniqueness, Ergodicity, and Teichm\"uller Complex Manifold Structure
item.description: arXiv:2611.08384v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Building on our previous work, in which geometric Gibbs measures were introduced to complete the space of classical Gibbs measures under the Teichm\"uller metric, we establish the uniqueness of geometric Gibbs measures in this paper. This result completes the construction of a Teichm\"uller complex manifold structure on the space of all geometric Gibbs measures. Using the welding technique, we uncover a connection between geometric Gibbs measures and harmonic measures on dynamical quasicircles. This connection allows us to establish asymptotic conformal rigidity for these dynamical quasicircles. Finally, we establish a foundation for the systematic study of the ergodic properties of geometric Gibbs measures.
item.dc:creator: Yunping Jiang

item.title: Averages of sub-additive functions through non-F{\o}lner sequences
item.description: arXiv:2611.08408v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the quantity $\sup_{\phi\in\Phi}\limsup_{n\to\infty}\phi(F_n)/|F_n|$, where $\mathcal F= (F_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ is a sequence of finite subsets of a countable amenable group, and $\Phi$ is a collection of subadditive functions. Under mild conditions on $\Phi$ we prove that the aforementioned quantity equals the supremum over $\phi\in\Phi$ of the limit of $\phi(F)/|F|$ as $F$ becomes more and more invariant, multiplied by a ``F{\o}lnerness'' constant $C(\mathcal F)\in[1,\infty]$. We have $C(\mathcal F)=1$ if and only if $\mathcal F$ is F\o lner. A corollary of this result is that every choice of a non-F\o lner sequence overestimates topological and measure-theoretic entropy by the multiplicative factor $C(\mathcal F)$ (in the positive entropy case). We obtain a generalization of classical results of Goodman, Krug, and Newton, on the so-called proportionality principle for sequence entropy, and their extension by Gao, Huang, and Zhu to countable amenable groups.
item.dc:creator: Nicanor Carrasco-Vargas

item.title: h-dichotomies via noncritical uniformity and expansiveness for noninvertible evolution families
item.description: arXiv:2611.08451v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish characterizations of h-dichotomies for noninvertible evolution families acting on Banach spaces, in terms of appropriate notions of expansiveness and uniform noncriticality. Our results extend the corresponding characterizations previously obtained for invertible evolution families. To the best of our knowledge, no such characterizations have previously been established for general noninvertible evolution families. A key difference is that noninvertibility makes the structure of the stable spaces more delicate: in our positive-half-line result, finite codimension must be imposed at every time, rather than only at the initial time. We show by an example that the latter, weaker condition is insufficient. We also study evolution families on the negative half-line, using duality to obtain corresponding characterizations in terms of dual expansiveness and dual uniform noncriticality. General growth rates are treated by a time-rescaling argument.
item.dc:creator: Davor Dragicevic

item.title: Periodic counting, carry synchronization, and primes in nonstandard numeration systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.07446v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $b\ge2$ be an integer and let $D\subset\mathbb{N}_0$ be a finite digit set containing zero, with maximum residue multiplicity $\mu=\max_{0\le r<b}\#\{d\in D:d\equiv r\pmod b\}$ and cardinality $q=\#D\ge2$. Under the condition $\mu<q$, we prove that the summatory representation function satisfies an asymptotic formula with a strictly positive, H\"older continuous, $1$-periodic fluctuating profile and an error of $O_D(x^{\log_b\mu})$. An exact periodic factorization of the Laplace generating function furnishes an explicit, computable Fourier expansion for the periodic profile via Gamma factors, and yields the meromorphic continuation of the associated Dirichlet series to the entire complex plane. When $D$ is a complete residue system modulo $b$, we establish an arithmetic synchronization criterion showing that the associated finite carry system admits a zero-synchronizing word if and only if $\gcd(D)=1$. This synchronization yields an exponentially accurate interval approximation and a general transfer principle for arithmetic weights. Consequently, we derive a prime number theorem for representable primes governed by the same periodic profile, alongside an exponentially convergent measurable scaling limit of the representable sets.
item.dc:creator: Nian Hong Zhou

item.title: Multivariable Congruence Jumping: Periodic States, Integral Realizations, and Descent
item.description: arXiv:2611.07625v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Congruence jumping replaces coordinates by integer quotients and updates polynomial divisibility relations. We extend this procedure to several variables and retain integer coefficients by recording their common factor separately. For three-variable systems of divisibilities with signed binomial numerators, we classify all positive integer exponent tuples of period at most two under three successive coordinate jumps: seven fixed tuples and twenty-two cycles of exact period two. No odd period greater than one occurs. At the chosen representatives of the twenty-two exponent two-cycles, there are eighty-four returning sign assignments. All have realizations with nonzero pairwise-coprime integer coordinates, and exactly seventy-four have such realizations with every coordinate positive throughout the six jumps. Explicit constructions and congruence arguments establish this classification. We also study jumps that decrease a specified height, distinguishing points that admit no immediate decrease from minima of entire connected components of the jump graph. For the four-variable family $Q_\lambda(x,y,z,w)=kxyzw$, where $Q_\lambda$ is the sum of the four squares plus $\lambda$ times the six pairwise products, finite bounds give complete classifications for $\lambda=1,2,3$. For $\lambda=1$, positive integer solutions exist exactly for $k=2,8,10$. These results distinguish returns of the polynomial data from integrality and positivity of the coordinate sequences.
item.dc:creator: Max A. Alekseyev, Dmitry I. Khomovsky

item.title: Density and holes of the visible points in certain cut-and-project sets
item.description: arXiv:2611.08257v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the set of visible points from the origin in certain cut-and-project sets, specifically the density of the set. We generalize to all real quadratic number fields the formulas for the density found by G. Hammarhjelm, and the corresponding error bounds proved by I. Gringlaz, R. Kumar, B. Weiss. We also find the possible densities of the set of visible points in the cut-and-project set, with a constant generic lattice, and a changing window with constant volume. We also study bounds for the distance of large holes in the set of visible points of certain cut-and-project sets, generalizing theorems originally proved by P. Erd\H{o}s for $\mathbb{Z}^2$.
item.dc:creator: Hayim David Shamir

item.title: Data-driven discovery of intrinsic Lie point symmetries of differential equation systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.08421v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Discovering continuous symmetries directly from differential-equation data can reveal geometric structure for model reduction and scientific machine learning without symbolic determining equations or a closed-form representation of the governing system. We formulate intrinsic Lie point-symmetry discovery as an operator-theoretic problem on sampled jet-space data. Admissible generators are identified from a sampled determining operator and separated from redundant, solution-dependent, and geometrically trivial directions. The framework combines prolongation, sequential subspace restrictions, and a fixed nonlinear dictionary linear in trainable coefficients. A rank-stabilization preflight test diagnoses systems whose represented intrinsic symmetry algebra does not stabilize under dictionary refinement. On a controlled differential-equation benchmark with an analytically known 11-dimensional represented intrinsic symmetry algebra, the method recovers the complete represented generator set, reproduces its Lie-bracket structure to numerical precision, and approximates a known generator beyond the training domain. Here we show that explicit intrinsic continuous-symmetry generators can be recovered from data obtained from exact or approximate differential systems.
item.dc:creator: Ilker Gurcan, Kadir Ustun, Ramazan Gokberk Cinbis

item.title: Semigroups of matrices with dense orbits (revised version)
item.description: arXiv:0905.1311v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For $\mathbb{K}=\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and every $n\ge 1$ we construct two $n\times n$ matrices $A$ and $B$ such that the orbit of every vector $p\in\mathbb{K}^n$ with $p_1\ne 0$ under the semigroup generated by $A$ and $B$ is dense in $\mathbb{K}^n$; the remaining vectors lie in an invariant hyperplane, so the set of vectors with dense orbit is exactly the complement of a hyperplane. Thus two generators always suffice for a hypercyclic semigroup of matrices, in contrast with the commutative case, where $n+1$ generators are needed on $\mathbb{C}^n$. We give a transparent reformulation of the hypotheses, a criterion for the density of $\{a^mb^n\}$ that makes them checkable, and explicit examples with complete proofs. As applications we obtain affine pairs on $\mathbb{K}^n$ all of whose orbits are dense, and, for every $n$, a pair of real matrices with an orbit that is somewhere dense but not dense in $\mathbb{R}^n$.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: M. Javaheri, Semigroups of matrices with dense orbits, Dyn. Syst. 26 (2011), no. 3, 235--243
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Javaheri

item.title: Maximally transitive semigroups of $n\times n$ matrices (revised and extended version)
item.description: arXiv:1201.0192v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mathbb{K}=\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. We prove that for every $n\ge 1$ there is a pair of $n\times n$ matrices with entries in $\mathbb{K}$ that generates a dense subsemigroup of the space $M_n(\mathbb{K})$ of all $n\times n$ matrices. Since the powers of a single matrix are never dense, two generators is optimal. Equivalently, there is a $2$-generator semigroup of linear maps whose action on $(\mathbb{K}^n)^n$ is topologically transitive, whereas no semigroup of linear maps acts topologically transitively on $(\mathbb{K}^n)^{n+1}$. In fact, for such a semigroup every orbit closure in $(\mathbb{K}^n)^k$, for every $k\ge1$, is as large as linear algebra allows. Along the way we give a short self-contained proof of the density of explicit $2$-generator subsemigroups of $GL_2^+(\mathbb{R})$ and of $M_2(\mathbb{R})$, based on a simple criterion for closed subsemigroups of $SL_2(\mathbb{R})$.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: M. Javaheri, Maximally transitive semigroups of nxn matrices, J. Math. Anal. Appl. 401 (2013), 743--753
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Javaheri

item.title: On a metric view of the polynomial shift locus
item.description: arXiv:2311.11399v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a path metric $\rho_D$ on the shift locus $\mathcal{S}_D$ of degree $D\geq2$ complex polynomials by connecting complex dynamics to geometric group theory. We encode the escape and deformation data of polynomial basins by metric graphs and use the thermodynamic geometry of the resulting metric graph space. We prove that $(\mathcal{S}_D,\rho_D)$ is complete if and only if $D=2$. For $D\geq3$, we show that the positive-height part of the metric boundary is naturally homeomorphic to the projectivized DeMarco--Pilgrim space $\mathbb{P}\mathcal{S}\mathcal{T}_D^*$. Our result provides a new way of understanding this space which encodes the topology of the shift locus and is defined abstractly as a monotone-light quotient.
item.dc:creator: Yan Mary He, Hongming Nie

item.title: Connection of hypocoercivity and hypocontractivity via the Cayley transform
item.description: arXiv:2601.09656v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The concepts of hypocoercivity and hypocontractivity and their relationship are studied for semi-dissipative continuous-time and discrete-time evolution equations in a Hilbert space setting. New proofs for the characterization of the short-time decay of the solution from the initial value are presented, that in particular characterize the constants in the leading terms of the solution when expanded in time. It is shown that the hypocoercivity index is equal to the hypocontractivity index when the implicit midpoint rule (the Cayley transformation) is used for the discretization. Maximally coercive/contractive representations of hypocoercive and hypocontractive semi-dissipative systems are presented, as well as the effect of different representations on the error estimates for the numerical solution.
item.dc:creator: Anton Arnold, Stefan Egger, Volker Mehrmann, Eduard A. Nigsch

item.title: Metastability Landscapes in Nonlinear Ghost-Normal Scalar Fields
item.description: arXiv:2604.25635v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate finite time dynamics in nonlinear classical scalar field systems containing one ghost and one normal kinetic sector. Using a spacetime finite element formulation, we study the dependence of threshold crossing and numerical continuation times on initial amplitude, characteristic wavenumber, spectral tilt, phase structure, and spatial localization. In the quartic model, larger amplitudes generally lead to earlier growth, while higher wavenumbers and ultraviolet-biased spectra favor longer resolved bounded evolution. Smooth compact initial data exhibit a broad region with no observed growth threshold crossing over the simulated interval. A direct comparison of two Gaussian evolutions shows that enhanced low-wavenumber power can precede rapid field growth, although this observation does not establish a universal spectral-transfer mechanism. We also compare the quartic interaction with a lifted $\phi^6$ potential. The latter gives a markedly different continuation landscape, with a broad long-converged region followed by shorter accessible terminal times at larger amplitudes. Localization diagnostics do not identify a persistent oscillon core in the selected cases. By distinguishing amplitude growth, spectral reorganization, solver-limited termination, and finite-time censoring, our results characterize a nontrivial metastability landscape without implying global or quantum stability.
item.dc:creator: Jax Wysong, Samara Overvaag, Hyun Lim, Jung-Han Kimn

item.title: On the First Caustic of Elliptical Billiards
item.description: arXiv:2606.04132v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A point source of light is placed inside a billiard with a smooth, convex, closed boundary. For any integer $n$, the $n$-th caustic by reflection, denoted by $\Gamma_n$, is the envelope of light rays that have undergone $n$ reflections in such a billiard after emanating from the source. It has been conjectured by Gil Bor and Serge Tabachnikov that for an elliptical billiard, $\Gamma_n$ has exactly four ordinary cusps; this problem is a billiard variation of Jacobi's Last Geometric Statement, which concerns the number of cusps in the conjugate locus of a point on an ellipsoid. Gil Bor, Mark Spivakovsky, and Serge Tabachnikov have proven that $\Gamma_n$ has at least four ordinary cusps. In this paper, we present a proof that $\Gamma_1$ has exactly four ordinary cusps, using billiards in complex spaces.
item.dc:creator: Aleksandra Uskova

item.title: Thermodynamic formalism for non-compact systems with expansivity and specification
item.description: arXiv:2606.20405v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a new theory of thermodynamic formalism for non-compact flows, providing criteria for existence and uniqueness of equilibrium states, as well as ergodicity and a Gibbs property. These criteria include new versions of the expansivity and specification properties that hold for geodesic flows on non-compact negatively curved manifolds. Previous results on thermodynamic formalism for these geodesic flows were restricted by a pinched curvature condition, which we remove, allowing curvature to approach both $0$ and $-\infty$. Our results also apply to geodesic flows beyond the smooth setting, including locally CAT(-1) spaces.
item.dc:creator: Vaughn Climenhaga, Daniel J. Thompson, Tianyu Wang

item.title: Exponential Consensus and Flocking in Multi-Agent Systems with Infinite Fading Memory
item.description: arXiv:2609.02454v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study the emergent collective dynamics of multi-agent systems driven by infinite distributed fading memory of Volterra type. We establish a unified theoretical framework covering both first-order opinion consensus dynamics and second-order velocity alignment flocking kinematics. By introducing Dafermos past-history transformations, the governing integro-differential systems are reformulated into dynamical systems on extended product Hilbert spaces. For first-order dynamics, we prove that fading memory inherently provides a hidden dissipative mechanism, guaranteeing unconditional global exponential consensus with or without instantaneous communication forces. For second-order dynamics, by developing a unified energy-multiplier framework that seamlessly couples instantaneous communication with memory dissipation, we establish unconditional global exponential flocking for both the pure fading memory system and the mixed interaction system, completely independent of the spatial dispersion or the communication tail.
item.dc:creator: Cristina Pignotti, Yu-Qing Wang

item.title: Slow Entropy of Quasi-Unipotent Actions on $S$-Arithmetic Homogeneous Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.39722v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study metric and topological slow entropy for translations on a class of finite-volume $S$-arithmetic homogeneous spaces with real and non-Archimedean factors. We consider translations whose real component is quasi-unipotent and whose non-Archimedean component lies in a compact open subgroup. At polynomial scales, we show that the metric and topological slow entropies coincide and are determined by the chain structure of the real adjoint action. In particular, the non-Archimedean component contributes no additional polynomial slow entropy. Our result extends the slow entropy formula of Kanigowski, Vinhage, and Wei for quasi-unipotent flows on real homogeneous spaces to this $S$-arithmetic setting.
item.dc:creator: Jasurbek Imomov

item.title: Dense 2-generator subsemigroups of $2\times 2$ matrices (revised and extended version)
item.description: arXiv:1104.5054v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that the semigroup of real linear fractional transformations of a proper subinterval of the real line does not contain a dense subsemigroup generated by two elements, while it does contain dense subsemigroups generated by three elements. For the semigroup generated by the two maps $x\mapsto 1+a/x$ and $x\mapsto x/b$ (the only pair not excluded by elementary arguments) we compute the closure exactly, and we describe all of its orbit closures in the plane. Consequently the semigroup of $2\times2$ matrices with nonnegative entries has no dense $2$-generator subsemigroup but has dense $3$-generator ones. In contrast, we prove a general density criterion for subsemigroups of $M_2(\mathbb{R})$ and $M_2(\mathbb{C})$ generated by three explicit matrices, and use a word identity of length seven to produce, for both $\mathbb{R}$ and $\mathbb{C}$, uncountable families of pairs of matrices that generate dense subsemigroups; a fully explicit rational example is $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&1/2\\1&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ and $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&0\\0&-8/3\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. Thus the minimal number of generators of a dense subsemigroup is $3$ for the nonnegative cone and $2$ for $M_2(\mathbb{R})$ and $M_2(\mathbb{C})$.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: M. Javaheri, Dense 2-generator subsemigroups of 2x2 matrices, J. Math. Anal. Appl. 387 (2012), 103--113
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Javaheri

item.title: Averaging principle for rough slow-fast systems of level 3
item.description: arXiv:2504.03110v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The averaging principle for slow-fast systems of various kind of stochastic (partial) differential equations has been extensively studied. An analogous result was shown for slow-fast systems of rough differential equations driven by random rough paths a few years ago and the study of ``rough slow-fast systems" seems to be gaining momentum now. In all known results, however, the driving rough paths are of level 2. In this paper we formulate rough slow-fast systems driven by random rough paths of level 3 and prove the strong averaging principle of Khas'minskii-type.
item.dc:creator: Yuzuru Inahama

item.title: Heavy repulsion of clusters in Bernoulli percolation
item.description: arXiv:2509.10631v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider Bernoulli$(p)$ percolation on (non)unimodular quasi-transitive graphs and prove that, almost surely, for any two clusters $C$ and $C'$, the set of vertices in $C$ within distance one of $C'$ is light, i.e.\ it has finite total modular weight. This is a significant step towards resolving a longstanding question of H\"aggstr\"om, Peres, and Schonmann, and a generalization of a theorem of Tim\'ar, who proved the same result in the unimodular setting. We present two proofs. The first one is a hyperfiniteness argument that is specific to Bernoulli$(p)$ percolation and is new even in the unimodular case; the second is more general and follows Tim\'ar's approach, but requires the development of weighted analogues of several classical unimodular results. The new insight in both proofs is nonhyperfiniteness, which we obtain from the recently developed theory of measure class preserving equivalence relations and graphs. In particular, along the way we establish a generalization of a theorem of Benjamini, Lyons, and Schramm on the existence of an invariant random subgraph with positive weighted Cheeger constant, which is of independent interest.
item.dc:creator: Sasha Bell, Tasmin Chu, Owen Rodgers, Grigory Terlov, Anush Tserunyan

item.title: Generalized Hausdorff measure of irrationals with Lagrange value exactly 3
item.description: arXiv:2511.10328v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the generalized Hausdorff measure of some natural subsets of $k^{-1}(3)$, where $k^{-1}(3)$ consists of the real numbers $x$ for which $\left| x-\frac{p}{q} \right|<\frac{1}{(3+\varepsilon)q^2}$ has infinitely many rational solutions $\frac{p}{q}$ for any $\varepsilon<0$ but only finitely many for any $\varepsilon>0$. It is well known that $k^{-1}(3)$ is an uncountable set with Hausdorff dimension zero. Given any dimension function $h$, we determine the exact ``cut point" at which the generalized Hausdorff measure $\mathcal{H}^h(k^{-1}(3))$ drops from infinity to zero. In particular we show that such a measure is always zero or not $\sigma$--finite, and, as an application, we can classify topologically $k^{-1}(3)$. Moreover, we show that the subset of attainable elements of $k^{-1}(3)$ has the same generalized Hausdorff measure as $k^{-1}(3)$, but the subset of non--attainable elements of $k^{-1}(3)$ has a ``strictly smaller" generalized Hausdorff measure.
item.dc:creator: Carlos Gustavo Moreira, Harold Erazo, Nicolas Angelini

item.title: Dynamics in large scale geometry
item.description: arXiv:2604.24452v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate the large scale geometry of certain metric spaces through the lens of dynamics. Our approach establishes a close connection between large scale dynamical phenomena and operator algebras by characterizing various large scale dynamic behaviors in terms of GNS representations of the uniform Roe algebras arising from natural canonical states. Our dynamical systems are given by the Stone-\v{C}ech boundary of metric spaces together with their inverse semigroup of partial translations. This defines a space of orbits and we characterize Hausdorffness and $T_1$-ness of this space by the failure of coarse embeddability of certain metric spaces. Surprisingly, while the orbit space has very weak separation properties, we show that it satisfies a certain ''localized version'' of Urysohn's lemma. We show that the topology of the space of orbits and quasi-orbits are given by the space of irreducible representations of uniform Roe algebras and by the space of their primitive ideals, respectively. As a highlight of the theory developed herein, we provide classes of spaces such that the prime ideals of their uniform Roe algebras are primitive. This is the case for instance of spaces whose orbit space is $T_1$.
item.dc:creator: Bruno de Mendon\c{c}a Braga, Alcides Buss, Ruy Exel

item.title: Scaling Symmetries and Conformal Relative Equilibria on Poisson Manifolds, with Applications to Lie-Poisson Systems
item.description: arXiv:2605.09062v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate conformal relative equilibria for Hamiltonian systems on exact Poisson manifolds equipped with scaling symmetries. By introducing conformally Poisson actions and conformal momentum maps, we characterize these equilibria through an augmented Hamiltonian formulation; in the nondegenerate case, this recovers the conditions recently developed for the exact symplectic case. Specializing to the Lie-Poisson manifold $\mathfrak g^*$ associated with an arbitrary finite-dimensional real Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, we show that its natural scaling action makes $\mathfrak g^*$ an exact Poisson manifold. We then establish a purely algebraic existence criterion: there exists a homogeneous Hamiltonian on $\mathfrak g^*$ admitting a nontrivial conformal relative equilibrium if and only if $\mathfrak g$ contains an element whose adjoint operator has a nonzero real eigenvalue. Applying this criterion to the Bianchi classification, we identify exactly the real three-dimensional Lie algebras for which there exists a homogeneous Hamiltonian admitting a nontrivial conformal relative equilibrium. As a prominent application, we show that nontrivial conformal relative equilibria exist for a rigid body on $\mathfrak{so}(2,1)^*$, whereas the classical free rigid body on $\mathfrak{so}(3)^*$ admits no nontrivial conformal relative equilibria.
item.dc:creator: Manuele Santoprete

item.title: On statistical inference for non-linear dynamical systems evolving in their global attractor
item.description: arXiv:2606.06018v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider a periodic scalar reaction-diffusion system over a two-dimensional domain under natural conditions on the reaction function and with initial condition $\theta$. We show that on the global attractor $\mathcal A$ of the resulting dynamical system $(u_\theta(t):t>0)$, a reverse Poincar\'e inequality holds true, and that as a consequence the map $\theta \mapsto u_\theta(t)$ satisfies an $L^2(\Om)$-Lipschitz stability estimate on $\mathcal A$ for any $t>0$ fixed. We then show that statistical recovery of an initial condition $\theta$ in the attractor $\mathcal A$, as well as prediction of the states $u_\theta$, is possible from discrete measurements of the system at parametric $1/\sqrt N$ convergence rates.
item.dc:creator: Dimitri Konen, Richard Nickl

item.title: Foliated and Mather-Jacobian discrepancies via tangential arcs
item.description: arXiv:2607.01809v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We express the log discrepancies of co-rank one foliations on normal varieties in terms of arc codimensions and differential orders. On smooth threefolds, if a foliation has simple singularities and its separatrices form an algebraic simple normal crossings divisor, we identify its foliated discrepancies with those of an ordinary pair for every divisor centred on the separatrices. This gives adjunction and log canonical threshold formulae. For algebraic images of the separatrices, we estimate changes in boundary orders caused by failure of ideal generation and by descent through the conductor. For locally complete intersection images, comparison on a common resolution yields criteria for equality of discrepancies and bounds on log canonical thresholds.
item.dc:creator: Maur\'icio Corr\^ea

item.title: Curvature-Dependent Path Concentration in Stochastic Fast-Slow Systems with Noise on the Slow Variable
item.description: arXiv:2607.16217v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study stochastic fast-slow systems with noise acting exclusively on the slow variable near uniformly attracting, normally hyperbolic critical manifolds $x=X^\ast(y)$. The deviation equation contains transmitted diffusion and an It\^o curvature forcing of order $O(\sigma^2\lVert D^2X^\ast\rVert)$. Using a parameter-dependent Lyapunov function and stopped martingale estimates, we obtain geometry-dependent concentration bounds under the sufficient noise restriction $\sigma\le C_0\min(\sqrt{\varepsilon},\varepsilon^{1/4}L_{\mathrm{geom}}/\sqrt{\lambda_0})$, where $\lambda_0$ is the uniform spectral gap and $L_{\mathrm{geom}}=\sqrt{\lambda_0/(\lVert D^2X^\ast\rVert\lVert h\rVert^2)}$. For fixed geometry and any fixed $p>0$, the confidence radius on $[0,T/\varepsilon]$ is $O(\varepsilon+\sigma^2+\sigma\sqrt{\log(1/\varepsilon)})$, with stopped fast-variable failure probability at most $\varepsilon^p$; slow-variable exit is controlled separately. We also establish an adiabatic error bound of order $O(\varepsilon+\sigma\sqrt{\varepsilon}+\sigma^2\lVert D^2X^\ast\rVert)$, with explicit failure probabilities. These estimates quantify the curvature dependence of fast-variable concentration and its $O(\varepsilon)$ contribution to the slow-error upper bound for fixed geometry.
item.dc:creator: Yefan Wu

item.title: Networked Admissibility-Preserving Control for Directed Safe Coordination
item.description: arXiv:2609.09384v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper addresses safe coordination of scalar agents with constrained input dynamics over fixed rooted digraphs. We propose a networked Admissibility-Preserving Control (APC) architecture for a common moving output corridor under heterogeneous asymmetric input bounds, wherein the Admissibility-Preserving Input Realization (APIR) generates the physical inputs. In logarithmic barrier coordinates, the closed-loop dynamics form an exact cascade of exponentially decaying realization errors and directed consensus dynamics. We derive direction-specific compatibility conditions that guarantee uniform corridor and input margins, bounded commands, unique complete solutions, and exponential consensus for compact initial sets. The closed-form expression for the agreement value quantifies the effect of the initial APIR mismatch. Under the corresponding compatibility conditions, partial pinning guarantees safe reference tracking whenever the root component contains at least one informed agent. Simulations illustrate the coordination guarantees.
item.dc:creator: Abhinav Sinha, Lohitvel Gopikannan, Shashi Ranjan Kumar

item.title: Stability of Diophantine Minimal Foliations in Arbitrary Codimension
item.description: arXiv:2610.15984v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We generalize Moser's stability theorem for minimal hypersurface foliations to arbitrary codimension. Let $\mathbb{T}^N=\mathbb{R}^N/\mathbb{Z}^N$ be the standard torus, and let $P\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ be an $m$-plane satisfying a Diophantine condition relative to $\mathbb{Z}^N$. We prove that, under every sufficiently small smooth $\mathbb{Z}^N$-periodic perturbation of the Euclidean metric, the affine foliation of $\mathbb{T}^N$ induced by $P$ persists as a smoothly conjugate foliation by minimal $m$-dimensional submanifolds. The normalized conjugating displacement depends smoothly and tamely on the metric and is locally unique. Moreover, the perturbed foliation admits a common smooth calibration, hence the lifted leaves are area-minimizing. The proof uses Hamilton's formulation of the Nash-Moser implicit function theorem.
item.dc:creator: Hoan Nguyen

item.title: $2$-Large Sets and Nil-Bohr Recurrence: A Disproof of the $2$-Large Is Large Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.16605v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A set $S$ of positive integers is $r$-large if every $r$-coloring of $\mathbb{N}$ contains arbitrarily long monochromatic arithmetic progressions with common difference in $S$. We prove that every $2$-large set is a set of nil-Bohr recurrence, i.e., it meets every nil-Bohr neighborhood of $0$. This proves a conjecture of the first author and gives a sharp answer to a question of Host, Kra, and Maass. Furthermore, we show that a piecewise syndetic set is $2$-large if and only if it is nil-Bohr recurrent. From this, we show that a small modification of a set constructed by the first author is $2$-large but not $3$-large, thereby disproving the $2$-large is large conjecture of Brown, Graham, and Landman. We also deduce that the family of $2$-large sets is not partition regular, thereby answering another question of Brown, Graham, and Landman. We also show that, for every fixed nil-Bohr neighborhood $B$ of $0$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, restricting the common difference to $B$ increases the extremal number for $k$-term arithmetic progressions by at most a factor of $1+\varepsilon$, provided $k$ is sufficiently large.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Alweiss, Sohail Farhangi

item.title: PCF All The Way Down
item.description: arXiv:2611.06106v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that a finite surjective post-critically finite self-map of a variety in characteristic zero remains post-critically finite on every preperiodic integral effective divisor after passing to its periodic image with its return map. Iterating this result proves PCF all the way down. A detailed report on AI usage is contained in the manuscript.
item.dc:creator: Taylor Dupuy, Alon Levy, Thomas Tucker, Zhuoran Wang
